threads.body: The `awk` range extraction can bleed across multiple PR bodies if any open module-cleanup PR is missing the terminating `---` line. `gh pr list --jq '.[].body'` outputs bodies back-to-back with no explicit separator, so once `f` is set it will continue scanning into subsequent bodies until it finds a later `---`, potentially reintroducing the processed-set poisoning this is trying to prevent. Consider parsing each body independently (e.g., do the section extraction in `jq` per element), or add an explicit sentinel delimiter between bodies in the `--jq` output and have `awk` reset `f` on that delimiter.
threads.hunk:
@@ -131,10 +131,13 @@ jobs:
           # bodies list the modules under "## Modules in this batch" as
           # "- " followed by the short wrapped in backticks). Once a PR
           # merges, those shorts also exist in processed.txt so they won't
-          # be re-picked.
+          # be re-picked. Only scan the "Modules in this batch" section
+          # (terminated by `---`) so an unrelated backticked line elsewhere
+          # in the body cannot poison the processed-set.
           inflight=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
                        --label "module cleanup" --state open \
                        --json body --jq '.[].body' \
+                     | awk '/^## Modules in this batch/{f=1; next} /^---/{f=0} f' \
                      | sed -n 's/^- `\([^`]*\)`$/\1/p' || true)

threads.body: The hidden per-module marker is derived from the commit subject (`%s`), but the module-cleanup persona requires subjects like `Cleanup for <module>`. That means these markers will currently include the `Cleanup for ` prefix and won’t match the `short_name` values in `processed.txt`/`REVIEW_PROGRESS`, so inflight PRs won’t be excluded and modules can be re-picked. Adjust the marker generation to emit just the raw module short name (e.g., strip the `Cleanup for ` prefix, consistent with the visible module list below).

threads.body: `--jq '.[].body | split("\n")[]'` will error if any PR has a null body (GitHub API can return `body: null`). Because the pipeline is `|| true`, this would silently drop all inflight markers and allow re-picking modules already in open PRs. Consider null-coalescing in jq (e.g., treat null as empty string) before splitting.
